title: Windows: Microsoft Pinyin switches from English mode to Chinese mode after running and stopping a project
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.8 dev4.
- Reproducible in Godot 4.8 dev3.
- Reproducible in Godot 4.7 stable.
- Reproducible in Godot 4.4.1 stable.
- This does not appear to be a recent Godot regression.



### System information

Godot v4.8.dev4 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors (3840x2160 @ 60.00 Hz, 3840x2160 @ 60.00 Hz) - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 61.55 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When using Microsoft Pinyin on Windows, after running and stopping a Godot project, clicking anywhere inside the built-in script editor can unexpectedly change Microsoft Pinyin from its internal English input mode (`英`) to Chinese input mode (`中`).

When the script editor is clicked, the Microsoft Pinyin status indicator may rapidly alternate between `中` and `英` several times before eventually remaining in `中`.


This is not a switch between different Windows keyboard layouts or input methods.

Microsoft Pinyin remains selected the entire time. The mode inside Microsoft Pinyin itself changes from English to Chinese.

For example:

1. Microsoft Pinyin is selected.
2. Its current mode is explicitly set to English (`英`).
3. A Godot project is run.
4. The running game is closed or stopped.
5. Microsoft Pinyin is now in Chinese mode (`中`) without the user manually switching the mode.

There is also another visible symptom after returning to the editor.

When clicking inside the built-in script editor after stopping the project, the Microsoft Pinyin status indicator can rapidly switch between `中` and `英` several times before eventually remaining in `中`.

This is particularly disruptive when editing GDScript because after testing the game, typing code may unexpectedly start a Chinese Pinyin composition instead of inserting ASCII text.



### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows 11, select Microsoft Pinyin as the current input method.
2. Switch Microsoft Pinyin itself to English input mode (`英`).
3. Open any Godot project.
4. Open a script in the built-in script editor.
5. Run the project.
6. Close or stop the running project.
7. Click anywhere inside the built-in script editor.
8. Observe the Microsoft Pinyin status indicator.

After clicking inside the script editor, the Microsoft Pinyin status indicator may rapidly alternate between `中` and `英` several times, eventually remaining in Chinese mode (`中`).

No keyboard shortcut for switching the IME mode is pressed during this process.


### Expected behavior

Running and stopping a project should not modify the current input mode of Microsoft Pinyin.

If Microsoft Pinyin was in English mode (`英`) before running the project, it should remain in English mode after focus returns to the Godot editor.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7944b894-c80d-4565-b9f8-e6dc9a6b920e

### Additional information

I originally suspected this was a regression in Godot 4.8 dev4, but further testing showed that the same behavior is reproducible in older Godot versions, including 4.4.1 stable.

I also tested Microsoft's legacy/compatibility version of Microsoft Pinyin.

With the legacy Microsoft Pinyin enabled, the automatic `英` -> `中` switch after running the project no longer occurs.

However, the legacy IME introduces a different compatibility problem specifically in Godot: Shift-modified symbols such as `#` (`Shift + 3`) become difficult or unreliable to type in the script editor.

I tested the same physical keyboard using the Windows English (US) keyboard layout instead of Microsoft Pinyin, and `Shift + 3` / `#` immediately works normally in Godot.

I also disabled the Microsoft Pinyin `Shift` shortcut for switching between Chinese and English modes, but this did not fix the `#` input problem with the legacy IME.

Therefore, the behavior appears to be related to the interaction between Godot and Microsoft Pinyin rather than a physical keyboard issue.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

No project-specific setup appears to be required.

The issue can be reproduced using a basic Godot project with any script opened in the built-in script editor.
